\caption{Every optimization, put back one at a time, on a 45~Mbp chromosome --- so these are \emph{relative} worths, not the whole-genome result, which is Figure~\ref{fig:vscpp}. \emph{pre-optimization} is this port with every ablatable change switched off (\texttt{SHMAP\_ABLATE}); each rung to the right switches exactly one more back on, so adjacent rungs differ by one change and nothing else. Getting from the C++ to \emph{pre-optimization} is worth a further 1.67$\times$, measured against both in one sitting rather than drawn here, because the C++ takes no \texttt{-x} and these rungs do. The two series are the two thread counts, and the gap between them is row~4; row~8 is not ablatable. Left: wall clock, median over 9 round-robin runs of the whole ladder, whiskers at min--max, so an unresolved step is visible as one. Right: peak resident set, log scale --- one worker's genome-sized accumulator hides under the index-build peak, \texttt{-@8} workers' copies do not. Every rung's mapping is byte-identical; the run fails otherwise. Numbers and per-stage timers in \texttt{figure\_ablation.tsv}; the decomposition against the C++ in \texttt{reconcile.tsv}.}
\label{fig:ablation}
